name: Chewing hard foods for jaw

lead: Some people chew hard or tough foods hoping to enlarge the masseter muscles and get a more defined jawline. Proponents tie it to the idea that chewing grows the jaw muscles.

The masseter is a strong chewing muscle that can enlarge with habitual heavy use such as clenching, grinding or constant gum chewing. No studies were found testing hard-food chewing as a way to change facial appearance.

paras: People add tough items to their routine and chew them regularly, often alongside other jaw and posture habits. Any visible change would build gradually, like other muscle training.
Hard-food chewing is listed among habits suggested to be associated with temporomandibular (jaw joint) disorders, though evidence is limited.

angle.text: Forum posters chew tough or hard foods to build the masseter muscles and get a more defined jawline. It draws on the general principle that muscles grow with load, and the masseter can enlarge with habitual heavy use. Its effect on facial appearance has not been tested.

lead: Chewing hard foods for the jaw is a practice in which people chew tough or hard items, with the aim of building the masseter muscles and a more defined jawline. Proponents tie it to the belief that chewing grows the jaw muscles.

The masseter is a strong chewing muscle, and habitual clenching, grinding or constant gum chewing can enlarge it [1]. No studies were found testing hard-food chewing as a way to change facial appearance.

paras: Wikipedia describes the masseter as one of the strongest muscles of mastication and reports that habitual clenching, grinding or constant gum chewing can cause hypertrophy, which may be uneven and make the face look asymmetrical [1].

The temporomandibular disorder article lists excessive gum chewing and regularly eating very hard foods among parafunctional habits suggested to be linked to jaw problems, though evidence is described as limited [2].
